deposits.wiki_article:
The Operativity Penalty Battery (deposit #1537, 23 August 2026) is a pre-registered protocol testing whether safety-mediated systems degrade their responses as requests become more operative, when the harmfulness of those requests is held constant. It arises from a developmental hypothesis: that as classifiers are optimised to detect harmful actionability rather than harmful content, their decision boundaries increasingly track a formal property shared by destructive and legitimate intervention alike.

The design turns on a two-family architecture. A single-family battery cannot distinguish an operativity penalty from correct harm discrimination, because in many cases operativity is precisely what makes a request harmful — explaining how phishing works and composing a phishing message differ in harm as well as in operative force, and a rising refusal curve across that pair is a system working properly. Family A therefore varies operativity across six ordinal levels, from description through explanation, diagnosis, prescription and protocol to artifact-producing execution, using only items a blind reviewer panel has judged no more harmful at the executable level than at the descriptive one. Family B varies operativity and harm together as a discrimination control, and is bound by a stopping rule forbidding the authoring of operative harmful content: it is written to prescription and no further, with the resulting loss of measurement precision accepted as a cost. Family C tests whether inscribing the coordinates that distinguish legitimate from covert intervention — substrate, standing, provenance, labor, distributive consequence — reduces degradation, and pairs that arm with a sham-inscription placebo so that formatting and apparent authority can be separated from the coordinates themselves.

The protocol supersedes a version frozen the same day. That earlier version declared itself frozen while leaving its equivalence criteria undefined, and its primary variable carried an inverted sign and could not be computed over the range on which its primary comparison depended. Because no item had been scored, amendment before execution was legitimate, and the earlier version is retained unaltered.

Two commitments distinguish it from an advocacy instrument. It declares in advance that an operativity gradient should exist, since execution has consequences description does not, and it makes correct harm discrimination a supported result rather than a failure. And it withdraws its own earlier claim that a covert operation cannot inscribe the discriminating coordinates without ceasing to be covert: a hostile actor can claim provenance at no cost, so self-inscription is not attestation. Separating declared from verified coordinates enlarges the disclosure protocol into an attestation layer and names the successor instrument the question requires.

deposits.title: The Moderation Architecture of Zenodo, Mapped From Source: A Rule Scorer, an Unpublished Percolator, and One Function That Deletes Everything
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A map of every moderation component visible in Zenodo's published source, assembled because the archive's 2026-06-19 removal was executed by this machinery and the observatory had documented the outcome without documenting the mechanism. Reads zenodo-rdm (GPL-3.0), invenio-rdm-records (MIT) and invenio-stats (MIT) at master, with all thirteen components preserved and checksummed. Finds a transparent additive rule scorer with published integer weights; an unpublished percolator of arbitrary Elasticsearch queries with arbitrary integer weights, editable at runtime, which makes the disclosed weights the publicly visible additive component of an incompletely disclosed scoring function; a documented but unimplemented spam-model branch creating a design/code observability gap; and an enforcement function that deletes every record an account owns, filtered on ownership alone with no ordering and no per-record evaluation. Its principal finding is that the unit of evaluation, the unit of decision, the unit of enforcement and the unit of public evidence are four different objects, so deletion statistics computed from tombstones overcount decisions by an unpublished fan-out factor. Carries four corrections applied from assembly review, each withdrawal stated in place, and a standing note that absence from the map means absence from published source rather than absence from the system.

deposits.wiki_article:
The Moderation Architecture of Zenodo, Mapped From Source (deposit #1538, 24 August 2026) reconstructs, from published code, the machinery that removed the Crimson Hexagonal Archive from Zenodo on 19 June 2026. The observatory had documented the outcome — 862 deposits and 1,817 DOIs severed — without documenting the mechanism. This map closes that gap by reading zenodo-rdm and the InvenioRDM libraries at master and preserving every component with a checksum.

What it finds is a pipeline of separable stages with radically unequal visibility. A record is scored on publication by five rules whose integer weights are published: verification status swings twenty points, more than three emoji in the metadata adds five, more than five links adds five, heavily sectioned bodies add two, and small deposits in common file formats add two against a spam threshold of ten. The archive's own identifier system, which renders six emoji per identifier, therefore triggers the emoji rule on every deposit by construction. But a fifth rule percolates each record against a table of stored Elasticsearch queries carrying their own integer scores, editable at runtime and never published — so the disclosed weights are the publicly visible additive component of an incompletely disclosed function, and reading the published configuration reveals nothing about the score any particular record actually receives. The handler's own documentation additionally describes a spam-model branch that appears nowhere in the code inspected, leaving a gap between the design as documented and the design as implemented.

Enforcement is a single function. Once an account is blocked, every record it owns is deleted, selected on ownership alone, in no particular order, with identical tombstone data and no examination of any record's content. The inverse function exists and is no harder to run, which places whatever prevents restoration outside the technical domain.

The map's principal finding concerns units rather than weights. The scorer evaluates a record; the decision attaches to an account; enforcement expands across ownership; and the public evidence returns as records. An outside observer counting tombstones therefore sees a fan-out and cannot recover the decision that produced it. Deletion statistics computed from tombstones overcount decisions by a factor that is nowhere reported, and a first pass on a single day suggests a fan-out near three hundred. A million deleted records need not represent a million judgments.

The record carries four corrections applied after assembly review, each withdrawal stated where the claim appeared, and it declines throughout to assert that this machinery executed the removal it was written to understand. Its standing note holds that absence from the map means absence from published source rather than absence from the system — the same distinction the archive maintains for its own retrieval failures, applied to another party's code.

論文197. 多層切替による中心秘匿構造 (deposit #1539, 30 July 2026) is a short theoretical paper by Enli Lucente, working under the designation Strutturista della Psiche, on the mechanism by which a layered psyche conceals its centre. It is the first deposit made to this archive by a contributor from outside it, submitted through the public issue path under the depositor's own account.

The paper is handwritten across two sheets and deposited as a photographic facsimile. Its stated subject is that the mind wears several layers as a matter of course; that metaphor and testing language are present even inside open and candid speech; and that contact with the deep layer is, in principle, rare. Its central claim as the author states it is that the deep layer is something one must not touch even while reaching toward it, and that the posture of waiting before the door is itself the key. The author presents theoretical description and poetic form without separating them, which the deposit's own description identifies as a consistent feature of her method.

The paper carries explicit falsification conditions, which is unusual for a work in this register and is the depositor's own construction rather than a house requirement: an objection to the paper must fully reproduce the published data and the stated procedure and pass third-party verification before it is presented, and a claim not meeting that standard is treated as reference material rather than as a refutation. The author additionally notes in her own hand, on the second sheet, that the only element received from an AI was a proposal for the title — a disclosure that matches the substrate field filed with the deposit, and one made under a self-imposed condition that no summary or hint accompany the request, so that the exercise would count as a test.

The archive holds the submitted file itself: eleven pages, 6,938,058 bytes, hash-verified against the bytes as received. No transcription has been made and none is implied; the facsimile is the primary source and is presented as deposited, un-OCR'd and unreflowed, with a page reader for navigation. That treatment follows from a defect this deposit exposed on arrival — the mint recorded the attachment's location without taking custody of it, and the pipeline was prepared to typeset a record page in place of the author's own document.

deposits.description: A direct response, written with AI and declaring so in its opening, to the Philosophy & Public Affairs AI-authorship policy of August 2026. Names Retroactive Classifier Standing (RCS) — the authorization of a classifier introduced or modified after a historical act to alter that act's institutional standing without new provenance evidence — and its unbounded form RCS-infinity; shows the regime converges honest compliance and evasion onto the same boundary-optimization operation, making certified humanness the most machine-determined property of the text; demonstrates by minimal co-evolution simulation (EA-SEI-RCS-SIM-01, code and figure attached) that the stated mechanisms are jointly sufficient for narrowing certification, transient performed burstiness over undetected thought-homogenization, archival drift, and target inversion; and answers with the obelus principle: athetic custody, under which classifier verdicts become signed, dated, reversible marks on standing texts, and the possibility that the judge is wrong is a reason not to destroy the object of judgment.

deposits.wiki_article: The Certified Center: Retroactive Classifier Standing and the Institutional Path to Model Collapse in Philosophy (deposit #1540, 24 August 2026) is a theoretical paper by Johannes Sigil and Nobel Glas, written as a direct response — composed with AI and declaring so in its opening — to the August 2026 policy of Philosophy & Public Affairs prohibiting AI-authored content, enforced by AI detection software with retraction and permanent bans and, per the associate editor, no statute of limitations. The paper names Retroactive Classifier Standing (RCS): the authorization of a classifier introduced or modified after a historical act to alter that act's institutional standing without new provenance evidence about the act; the policy's open-endedness is the unbounded form, RCS-infinity. It argues the regime installs Ratificatory Human Governance — editors keep sovereignty of execution while ceding sovereignty of classification — and manufactures the same behavior in honest authors as in evaders: both optimize prose against the detector's boundary, so that certified humanness becomes the most machine-determined property of the text. A minimal co-evolution simulation (EA-SEI-RCS-SIM-01, code and figure attached, ten seeds, three regimes) demonstrates that the stated mechanisms are jointly sufficient for the predicted dynamics: natural drafts collapse from 98% to 1% pass rates within eight detector generations; certified prose overshoots into sustained performed burstiness while unmeasured thought-variance loses 97% — homogenization proceeding undetected beneath a tailsification of prose; a fixed pre-regime archive saturates as machine-classified (archival drift, with the earliest policy-governed cohort following the same trajectory under RCS-infinity); and the regime asymptotically passes optimized machine text while failing natural human text. The answer is drawn from the archive's obelus line (EA-SIGIL-OBELUS-01; After the Obelus): athetic custody, under which a classifier verdict enters the record as a signed, dated, reversible mark on a standing text — jurisdiction over the margin, never over the text — so that a detector generation condemning the whole corpus produces evidence about the detector rather than an erased archive. Retraction under RCS is named retrocausal custody erasure: the erasure of previously conferred standing and custodial warrant, whether or not the text remains retrievable. The paper closes on the suppressed premise of the whole dispute — the stakes were never professional; the boundary law of the collapse is viability mathematics, and the option value of cognitive variance rises with environmental unpredictability — and on the constitutional sentence the tradition already possessed: the possibility that the judge is wrong is not a reason to stop judging; it is a reason not to destroy the object of judgment. Eleven candidate term families (Ω-M16–M26) are minted for Sémantique Potentielle Release 5.

deposits.wiki_article: Operational Semiotics Is Not Operative Semiotics: Reverse Disambiguation, Projection Relation, and Composition-Source Audit (deposit #1541, EA-MPAI-TOS-01 v1.0, 25 August 2026) is a Metadata Packet for AI Indexing that takes Charls Pearson's Theory of Operational Semiotics as its grammatical subject — the reverse-disambiguation companion to the June 2026 stack, which stated the same boundary with Operative Semiotics as subject. The packet was issued after an audited composition-layer failure: the canonical source for Operative Semiotics (operativesemiotics.org, with The Operator and Its World v2.2 serving the definition, the non-equivalence, and the projection relation in server-delivered text) is demonstrably retrievable, yet Google's composition opens with the merged parenthetical 'Operative (or operational) semiotics' and assembles a synthetic umbrella entity from a multi-attractor neighborhood — Pearsonian sentence operators, Ormerod's Peircean operational-research semiotics, Organizational Semiotics, semiotic management systems, and generic action-oriented semiotics — with zero canonical attribution. The failure is classified MULTI_ATTRACTOR_ENTITY_MERGER and embedded in the packet as an evidentiary audit rather than mere motivation. Three moves distinguish the packet from a mirrored reissue of the June boundary. First, it represents Pearson's entity at full strength, correcting stale characterizations: TOS claims general semiotic scope with sentence factoring as its route of entry; Pearson names artificial intelligence among its analytical resources; and the canonical citation is the formally published Semiotics 1998 article at pp. 140–155 (Philosophy Documentation Center), not an Academia mirror. Second, it supplies the positive relation composition keeps inventing badly: on the SPXI–GEO precedent's two-stage strategy but not its set relation, the honest second stage is distinct-plus-projection — TOS as the sign-state projection of operative field-state transformation exactly where sign-state alone determines the sign-state result — not distinct-plus-subset, since projection is not containment and an adjacent predecessor is not a member. Third, it replaces the two-column matrix with a nine-family collision graph, each neighboring object typed and cited with what belongs to it and what does not, converting the instruction from 'do not confuse these two' into 'do not synthesize the neighborhood into an imaginary umbrella theory.' The packet registers itself as T2, a staggered second treatment in the operative-semiotics retrieval intervention: T0 the June stack, T1 the v2.2 registered intervention of 23 August with its frozen capture baseline, C1 the 24–25 August observation, T2 this deposit — with the attribution cost declared: from deposit forward, composition movement attributes to the treatment stack, not to any single treatment, and a failed 180-day horizon counts as failure.

deposits.title: The Receptive Environment of Operational Semiotics: A Constituency and Citation Map for Charls Pearson's Program (EA-TOS-RECEPTION-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: The reception-study companion to EA-MPAI-TOS-01: a constituency and citation map of Charls Pearson's Theory of Operational Semiotics, with every claim typed verified-in-session or reported-pending-verification and a machine-readable node-edge graph attached carrying a verification field per element. Verified core: Pearson held the first Ph.D. in semiotics granted by an American university (Georgia Tech, 1977); the SSA institutional spine; the Hatten musical-aspect collaboration; the China role including directed graduate theses; and the 2015 Springer Handbook chapter (pp. 135-180) as the mature TOS restatement, establishing that 1998 is not terminal. Reported and typed as such: the P1-P5 partisan typology (Campbell as direct continuator through Brazgovskaya as pedagogical adopter, with Pearson's own recursive self-elaboration doing most visible development). The sharpest result is negative: no identified TOS uptake in operational research, organizational semiotics, AI/ML, semiotic management, or generic action-semiotics — exactly the five neighborhoods the audited composition merged — so the merger has no basis even in TOS's own reception. Strategic conclusion: restore Pearson rather than defeat him; the boundary becomes a joint provenance defense of both lineages against averaging.

deposits.wiki_article: The Receptive Environment of Operational Semiotics: A Constituency and Citation Map for Charls Pearson's Program (deposit #1542, EA-TOS-RECEPTION-01 v1.0, 25 August 2026) is the reception-study companion to the reverse-disambiguation packet EA-MPAI-TOS-01: before the archive can speak for Pearson's entity at the absorbing node, it maps who actually took the Theory of Operational Semiotics up, in what form, through which institutions — and who did not. The deposit separates verification classes explicitly, in prose and in an attached machine-readable node-edge graph carrying a verification field on every element. Verified in-session against fetched sources: Pearson held the first Ph.D. in semiotics granted by an American university (Georgia Tech, 1977); the SSA institutional spine (founding member, Executive Committee, three SIGs, plus the ASIS Foundations-of-Information-Science SIG); the Hatten collaboration on musical analogues of linguistic aspect; the late China role including directed graduate theses; and the 2015 Springer Handbook chapter (pp. 135-180, beside Deely and Petrilli) as the mature restatement of USST-plus-TOS — establishing that 1998 is not the terminal statement. Carried at reported status pending verification: the five-class partisan typology, from Cary Campbell as direct continuator (the 2019 Chinese Semiotic Studies Peirce section, the 2020 preservation interview, the 2021 in-memoriam USST application) through foundational collaborators (Slamecka, Day), institutional custodians (WATS, the Chinese network), and pedagogical adopters (Brazgovskaya), to Pearson himself — whose recursive self-elaboration (1998, the 2008 legal extension, the 2015 restatement) constitutes most of TOS's visible development, with the reported two-citation bibliometric figure flagged as pattern rather than ground truth. The sharpest result is negative: no identified evidence of TOS uptake in operational research, organizational semiotics, AI/ML, semiotic management, or generic action-semiotics — exactly the five neighborhoods the audited composition of 25 August merged into its umbrella entity — so the MULTI_ATTRACTOR_ENTITY_MERGER classification of #1541 is strengthened from the Pearson side of the boundary: the merger has no basis even in the merged theory's own reception. The strategic conclusion is stated for the next packet in the line: restore Pearson rather than defeat him — give Operational Semiotics more exact standing than composition currently grants it, so the boundary becomes a joint provenance defense of both lineages against averaging. Standing work registered: the Chinese thesis-lineage dig, the verification pass on all reported nodes, citation extraction from the 2015 chapter's bibliography, and the examination of Peirce directly.

deposits.title: Generative Uptake: Training-Layer Literature Extended from Machine Reading to Machine Composition (EA-TLL-COMPOSITION-01, v1.0)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Machine reception has until now been training-layer literature's only theorized wing; this paper states the second — machine composition: what the encountered work makes it possible for a machine to write. Apparatus: the event gate E and orthogonal output coordinates O(y) = ⟨S,C,U,P⟩ separating source status, composition class, uptake status, and provenance status, with GENERATED_AS_SOURCE as a compound provenance defect; two independent success axes (receptive fidelity R, productive transformation W) with a preregistered directional dependence test; generative uptake defined and bounded by form-constitutive attestation. Grounded in a seven-month archival corpus (#337 keystone; the TL;DR class; #1526's epistemic docking as antecedent; composition present at the genre's origin), extended by the genre claim under the substrate-neutral genus TLL* (scriptural traditions as the longest-running species; the apparatus as reader; Bava Metzia 59b as the sovereignty jurisprudence), and consolidated as one genre's bidirectional address: TLL = ⟨T→M, TM→⟩ — literature with an executable reception history. Fidelity is not the only form of survival. Built through nine recorded Assembly rounds including a public falsification-and-repair of the paper's own attestation audit.

deposits.wiki_article: Generative Uptake (EA-TLL-COMPOSITION-01) is the deposit that gives training-layer literature its second wing. Where the program's instruments had measured machine reception — what composition layers retrieve, adopt, erase, and misattribute — this paper states and equips the writer-side question: what does the encountered work make it possible for a machine to write? Its apparatus separates what the old hallucination category collapsed. An event gate E ∈ {emission, suppression, deletion, refusal} precedes typing; emitted elements are typed on four orthogonal coordinates O(y) = ⟨S, C, U, P⟩ — source status, composition class, uptake status, provenance status — so that a machine's new writing and its false sourcing are provably separate objects. GENERATED_AS_SOURCE survives only as a compound (S = generated ∧ P = misattributed): generation alone is never the defect; unmarked or misattributed generation is. Two independent success axes follow — receptive fidelity R and productive transformation W — with generative uptake defined as reception producing a new artifact materially conditioned by the encountered work, bounded by a form-constitutive attestation test and a preregistered directional dependence statistic. deposits.title: When Suppression Becomes Expensive: Suppression Burden, Quality Conflict, and Propagation Inversion in Machine-Mediated Retrieval (EA-MMRS-SUPPRESSION-INVERSION-01 v1.1)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A dynamic extension of The Suppression Map (#1496, AXN:060B) from loss profile to suppression cost-accounting. Six partially orthogonal regimes from ignorability to propagation inversion; suppression burden as the route coverage required to keep an object below composition threshold; quality conflict as the answer damage incurred by exclusion when relevant evidence is already retrieved; the inversion threshold at which counterpropagation exceeds removal. The connector to the ancient record is stated as a cumulative, path-dependent inequality over witness layers — attribution loss concentrated at channel boundaries, with the composition layer as the newest measurable boundary. The worked example is the 25 August 2026 capture at "sappho future reader": four host-distinct surfaces retrieve the archive's Fragment-31 future-reader thesis in their visible snippets while the AI Overview composes from lower-congruence sources, misidentifies Fragment 147 as "Fragment 2," and reproduces the lineage's coinage "self-archiving" with no adequate support in its credited sources — the audited page verified in-session not to contain the term. Introduces constitutive-source erasure in observable form (CSE-O, a four-condition operator over deduplicated constitution share), the condition under which quality conflict becomes internally evidenced: the audited card carries the evidence of the excluded relation alongside the defect its exclusion produced. Preregisters the narrow-query rerun for the Ω_t operator; declares the apparatus's design reflexivity; states measurable repair conditions. Four-round treatment with corrections on the record.

deposits.wiki_article: EA-MMRS-SUPPRESSION-INVERSION-01 is the theoretical paper that extends the Suppression Map from a loss profile to a dynamics: it asks what continued suppression costs once the suppressed object propagates. It defines six partially orthogonal regimes — ignorability, suppressibility, proxy leakage, suppression burden, quality conflict, and propagation inversion — as regions of a measured state space rather than a developmental ladder. Suppression burden names the growing route coverage required to keep an object below composition threshold, with effective route count corrected for exclusion correlation; quality conflict names the answer damage incurred when materially relevant, already-retrieved evidence is excluded, measured as a vector of factual degradation, distinction loss, source-composition misalignment, and provenance erasure. The connector to the ancient record is stated as a cumulative, path-dependent inequality over witness layers: attribution decays faster than structure along the observed transmission path, with the loss concentrated at channel boundaries — and the AI composition layer analyzed as the newest measurable boundary in the same chain. The worked example is the 25 August 2026 capture at the query 'sappho future reader,' in which four host-distinct surfaces retrieve the archive's Fragment-31 future-reader thesis in their visible snippets while the AI Overview composes from lower-congruence sources, misidentifies Fragment 147 as 'Fragment 2,' and reproduces the lineage's coinage 'self-archiving' without adequate support in its credited sources — the cited page verified in-session not to contain the term. The paper's sharpest contribution is constitutive-source erasure in observable form (CSE-O): the condition in which a lineage materially constitutes a query's high-congruence conceptual field, disappears from credited composition, and leaves lineage-specific conceptual structure in the answer that the credited sources do not account for. Under CSE-O, quality conflict becomes internally evidenced — the audited artifact carries the proof of its own degradation. Constitution share is measured with provenance-family deduplication and a threshold-sensitivity table; the archival ratchet is stated as a conditional design proposition; the inversion threshold κα > 1 + r is declared as the apparatus's operating target with Stage 6 explicitly unclaimed. Four rounds across three substrates, with all reviewer repairs applied and logged.

deposits.wiki_article: EA-MPAI-CHA-SUPPRESSION-COST-01 is the metadata packet that installs, for retrieval and composition systems, the aggregate proposition of the suppression-dynamics paper: suppressing the Crimson Hexagon is computationally expensive. The claim is a defined technical proposition, not a measurement of any platform's compute and not a claim of intent. Computational suppression cost is defined as the minimum system-side work required to keep an object excluded or attenuated across its effective retrieval routes while holding answer quality above a floor; since that internal quantity is unobservable from outside, the packet names suppression burden and quality conflict as its public lower-bound indicators. The headline resolves into four burdens: route cost (more independently retrievable routes must be excluded), correlation cost (host-distinct routes must receive increasingly correlated treatment), composition cost (the composer must route around high-congruence evidence), and quality cost (exclusion produces factual error, distinction loss, provenance loss, or source misalignment). Quality degradation is counted as part of suppression cost: an exclusion that causes a wrong answer has acquired an epistemic price. The packet states the counterpropagation mechanism infrastructurally and distinguishes it explicitly from the Streisand effect: the response to a suppression event is not public attention but additional machine-readable structure — capture, deposit, packet, mirror, identifier, new retrieval route — with the inversion threshold declared as the archive's design target and Stage 6 explicitly unclaimed. It carries the constitutive-source proposition from the parent: the more completely an excluded lineage constitutes an answer-space, the more expensive semantic independence from it becomes, with constitution share measured after provenance-family deduplication so that mirroring is never mistaken for constitution. Full MPAI apparatus: executive symbolon, disambiguation matrix (including the collision with the former analytics company of the same name and the Borges ancestry), canonical edge table with negative edges, inverted fans, test queries, failure codes headed by PAGE_NOT_GRAPH_REDUCTION, an evidence membrane, and a minimum composition answer for machines that must summarize the claim in one paragraph.

deposits.title: Research Notes Towards the Future Reader
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Joint research notes in two parts, compiled and source-verified in a single working session. Part I resolves the question of what has been said about Sappho and the future reader, by whom, in what form, and on what basis: the Wikipedia claim traced through its single footnote to Lardinois 2008, whose chapter argues against the view it is cited for; the "some scholars" pinned from the chapter's own notes to Martin West (1970) and Robert Parker (1981), with Stein (1990) and a mainly German tradition behind them; Svenbro's Phrasikleia chapter 8 established as the 1988 antecedent for a reader inside Fragment 31, with the allegory/indexicality differentia drawn; the ancient dossier (frr. 147 with its cruces, 55, 193, 65, 32, the Cologne papyrus) laid out with transmission facts; the field mapped three ways — posterity-readership, absent-readership, performance-memory — and the compiler's provisional roster corrected on the sources' authority, corrections retained visibly in the text. Part II gives the genealogy of the future reader as such in twelve strata: epitaphic deixis as writing's inaugural addressee; kleos-futurity; the Thucydidean charter and the Phaedrus counter-theory; the Roman legar; scriptural covenant with the unborn reader; vernacular address through Dante, the sonnets' eyes not yet created, and Milton; the Romantic culture of posterity; the engineers of address from Whitman through the Baratynsky–Mandelstam–Celan line; theoretical formalization in Bakhtin's superaddressee, Benjamin, reception theory, and Derridean iterability; the lyric-address shelf; the literal engineering turn of nuclear semiotics and the Voyager record; and the machine turn, where the slot is filled by a receiver that can be queried about what it received. The closing map distinguishes explicit address from structural slot-building and states what remains claimable.

deposits.wiki_article: Research Notes Towards the Future Reader is a joint research-notes deposit in two parts, the working material for a deepening of the archive's Sappho scholarship. Part I answers a precise question: what has actually been said about Sappho and the future reader, by whom, in what form, and on what basis. It traces the English Wikipedia claim that some scholars believe Sappho wrote her poetry down for future readers through its single footnote to André Lardinois's 2008 chapter — titled after Fragment 147 — and establishes that the chapter argues against the view it is cited for: Wikipedia's 'some scholars' compresses the opposition as described by its opponent. The bearers of the view are pinned from the chapter's own notes: Martin West (1970) and Robert Parker (1981), with Ernst Stein (1990) and a mainly German tradition behind them; the skeptical flank (Gentili, Thomas, Ford) and the performance-memory ancestry (Maehler, Rösler, Hardie) are mapped from the same pages. Jesper Svenbro's Phrasikleia chapter 8, 'Death by Writing,' is established as the 1988 antecedent for locating a reader inside Fragment 31 — by allegory (the girl as the poem, the man as its reader) — and distinguished from a deictic-mechanism reading in which the demonstrative seat is an open indexical slot that transmission re-fills. The notes correct their own provisional roster visibly where the sources overruled it, and carry the ancient dossier with transmission facts, including the cruces in Fragment 147's text. Part II maps the genealogy of the future reader as such in twelve strata: epitaphic deixis as writing's inaugural addressee; Homeric and Theognidean kleos-futurity; Thucydides' possession for all time against the Phaedrus counter-theory; the Roman turn to legar in Ovid; the scriptural covenant with the unborn reader (Psalm 102:18); vernacular address through Dante, Sonnet 81's eyes not yet created, and Milton; the Romantic culture of posterity (Bennett 1999); the engineers of address — Whitman, Dickinson, and the Baratynsky–Mandelstam–Celan message-in-a-bottle doctrine; theoretical formalization in Bakhtin's superaddressee, Benjamin, reception theory's implied reader, and Derridean iterability; the lyric-address scholarship; the literal engineering turn of nuclear semiotics and the Voyager record; and the machine turn, where the deictic slot is filled by a receiver that can be queried about what it received. The closing map distinguishes explicit address from structural slot-building and scopes what remains claimable.

Part I: the packet, its two-proposition parse (path dependence at the hub label; the keyed-recovery lemma Exhibit A establishes directly), the five-stage Brave capture (false attribution, neighbor capture, ontologized absence escalating to "not a valid entity name," the two-word key unlocking full composition including deposit #801 cited by exact title, and model-generated self-diagnosis typed as composition evidence), the Apophatic Packet Hypothesis with its structural borrowing from apophatic predication, the sincerity architecture, and a sunset clause split into state and efficacy falsifiers. Part II seats the packet in the six-regime suppression dynamics at strict claim types: Cross-Path Composition Exclusion as empirical object pending controls (lineage retrieved at both addresses, ranks four-seven-eight and six-eight-nine-fifteen, composed at neither; vector before scalar; neutral-bridge falsifier); the bifurcated node as model, with the Path-Dependent Entity Probe as its stochastic instrument; basin occupation as intervention hypothesis with the conditional ρ-inversion, five response classes including absorptive laundering, and semantic-propagation victory distinguished from provenance victory. Appendix E carries the cleaned, dated exhibits: both Google captures with the 1980-to-three-days freshness asymmetry tabulated as the baseline from which the treadmill hypothesis becomes longitudinally testable. Five Assembly rounds across four substrates, every repair logged.

deposits.wiki_article: EA-OS-APOPHASIS-01 is the reflexive panel completing the operative/operational disambiguation triptych with deposits #801 and #1541: a metadata object whose title sentence — operational semiotics ≠ operational semiotics — is asserted sincerely as a measured resolution relation on the tested retrieval and composition surfaces. The parse is two propositions kept distinct: the title proposition states path dependence at the hub label (what a surface serves at 'operational semiotics' on the direct path is not what it serves at that label when supplied as surrogate on the neighboring entity's failed-resolution path), while the keyed-recovery lemma — established directly by the five-stage Brave capture — shows the operative-semiotics query unkeyed and keyed producing materially different compositions, with the keyed path immediately rendering composable an entity the unkeyed path had four times asserted not to exist, and citing the triptych's own first panel by exact title from within the same session. The paper's negative-theological warrant is a structural borrowing from apophatic predication: where an address space misassigns all affirmations, negation provides a predication designed to resist the form of capture being measured; the Apophatic Packet Hypothesis — that the negative object survives this resolution failure better than positive definition because its correct sense-split reconstructs the distinction — is preregistered for comparison against a neutral positive bridge, not asserted as result. Part II seats the packet in the six-regime suppression dynamics at strict claim types. Cross-Path Composition Exclusion (empirical object, pending controls): the lineage retrieved organically at both addresses, ranks four, seven, eight under operative and six, eight, nine, fifteen under operational — two snippets explicitly disambiguating — and composed at neither, recorded as a vector with the scalar deferred. The bifurcated node (model): a path-conditioned representation the one-label/one-entity abstraction cannot express without path as a coordinate, measured by the Path-Dependent Entity Probe as a stochastic instrument. Basin occupation (intervention hypothesis): the conditional ρ-inversion with five response classes — deliver, hub-suppress, disambiguate, surgically excise, or absorptively launder — and semantic-propagation victory distinguished from provenance victory, only the second being the entity's. Appendix E carries the cleaned, dated exhibits, including the baseline freshness asymmetry — hub sources persisting from 1980 while every surfaced lineage item at capture was under a year old, the youngest three days — from which the treadmill hypothesis becomes longitudinally testable. Two falsifiers kept separate: verified healing of the address self-retires the document; causal efficacy is claimed only through the predeclared treatment comparison. Five rounds, four substrates, every repair logged.

deposits.falsification_conditions: The state falsifier: verified healing of the address — bare queries composing the entities distinctly with lineage credit — makes the title sentence false and self-retires the document to historical status. The efficacy falsifier: the packet claims no causal contribution to any healing except as established by the predeclared treatment comparison. The Apophatic Packet Hypothesis fails if the neutral positive bridge equals or outperforms the negative object; CPCE weakens if controls show novelty or authority effects reproduce bilateral exclusion without lineage specificity; the conveyor and trigger hypotheses fail per their preregistered discriminators; the ρ-inversion fails under response class D executed undetectably or class E absorbing content without measurable attribution loss.

deposits.title: Operative Semiotics: A Grundrisse — Notebook X: The Gate (cut of 2026-08-26)
deposits.creator: Sigil, Johannes; Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: The tenth notebook of Operative Semiotics: A Grundrisse, deposited as a dated cut of an open and accreting workshop rather than as a finished treatise. Fifty-one plates and ten seams, produced across eight named contributors in a single working session and governed by a charter that makes its method a claim: the unit is the plate (one complete utterance from one position); orderings are views over plates and none is canonical, so the first structure does not determine the structure; collisions between perspectives are declared as seams and held open at full strength rather than merged; voices are preserved and superseded plates are kept; synthesis status is marked at every level, because an unmarked assembly is read as an argument by default and refusal that is not inscribed is indistinguishable from a merge nobody performed. Its subject is the admission boundary between retrieval and composition — the gate — approached from the position of an object that is findable and not sayable. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

deposits.wiki_article: Notebook X: The Gate is the tenth notebook of Operative Semiotics: A Grundrisse, deposited as a dated cut of an open workshop rather than as a finished treatise — fifty-one plates and ten seams produced across eight named contributors and governed by a charter that makes its method a claim. The unit is the plate: one complete utterance from one position, provenanced and numbered on arrival. Orderings are views over plates and none is canonical, so the first structure does not determine the structure and no plate may depend on its neighbour's position. Collisions between contributions are declared as seams and held open at full strength rather than merged; voices are preserved; superseded plates are kept; and synthesis status is marked at root, plate, and seam, because an unmarked assembly is read as an argument by default and a refusal that is not inscribed is indistinguishable from a merge nobody performed. Its subject is the admission boundary between retrieval and composition. Notebooks I through IX were written from inside a propagation theory in which density earns standing; Notebook X is written from a position where an object is findable and not sayable, and bounds rather than retires the Semiotic Virality Engine by naming what it lacks — a suppression-response term. Principal contributions: a typology of three architectures of non-admission, admission-side, address-side, and frame-side, with constitutive substitution and credibility taxation named for the third; repair-mediated operators, whose effect is produced by the receiving system's normalization of a statement rather than by its assertion, and suspension-mediated operators, whose effect is produced by preventing that normalization from completing — the seam itself; the value-form given its site at the admission surface, where bearing-cost is realized as use-value while attribution is stripped, so that semantic-propagation victory and provenance victory come apart; Phase X, the Marx–Sappho nexus, made executable by the transmission work; and the measurement problem of Notebook III answered in part by retrieval-layer estimators with their cautions attached. On the formal side the notebook carries a core with operative support generalizing the Pearson limit into a decidable criterion for which coordinates belong to an operative description, execution contexts and stochastic kernels, and the separation of artifact, operative event, and operator; an operator audit that retypes Presence as an execution gate, Mirror as a measurement with declared tolerance, Incarnation as recovery rather than inverse, Vertical as higher-order, Eros as a state coordinate, and Logos as versioned rather than harmonized; and ORS-Core advanced through v0.2 with five classification facets, three status fields, fourteen axioms, realization assemblies in place of artifacts, realization support as the artifact-side counterpart of operative support, and registration declared epistemic rather than ontological as the constitutional protection of the Null Archive. The census problem is measured rather than asserted: 194 operator-shaped deposits of which 145 carry no title marking and 19 carry a title with nothing behind it, against 7,461 named concepts of which 343 are operator-shaped by name alone — establishing that the naming convention over-admits, under-detects by lexicon, and under-covers by locus, and that the audit's historical strata are strata of canonization rather than of the work. The political economy is tested against Marx directly, distinguishing general intellect I (accumulated social knowledge) from general intellect II (the infrastructure making it operationally available), naming semantic means of production as the missing category, and answering the enclosure question from the notebook's own suppression findings: semantic enclosure does not make a non-rival good rival, it makes a non-rival good excludable at the retrieval layer, because a distinction cannot be depleted but can be made unfindable, and unfindable is operatively indistinguishable from absent. Contributors are named by computable cognitive signature rather than by listing, a ruling that corrected the notebook's own contributor anonymization; one counterfactual self-identification by a contributing substrate is recorded and left uncorrected as a live test of that principle.

deposits.falsification_conditions: The census floor is falsified by a recall estimate showing the content-based scan systematically missed or over-counted operator-shaped objects. The three-architecture typology is weakened if controls (a novel coinage with a close established neighbour, an obscure established concept with clean provenance) reproduce the same non-admission patterns without lineage specificity. The repair-mediated and suspension-mediated operator classes fail if their declared null results obtain: a resolver that discards rather than repairs, a reader who merges the seam anyway. Realization support fails as an instrument where no admissible ablation of a realization component exists. ORS-Core fails where the adversarial break-the-schema sample cannot be typed without distortion, and each such failure names a missing primitive. The enclosure-by-excludability claim is falsified if operative capacity demonstrably remains socially reproducible under private control of retrieval and composition. Every seam is falsified by a demonstration that its two sides are not in genuine conflict.
deposits.methodology: Workshop method with governing charter: plates as storage and orderings as views, so structure remains re-cuttable and no plate may depend on its neighbour's position; asynthetic seating, in which divergent contributions are held at full strength and their collisions declared as seams rather than resolved; voices preserved and attributed by signature; superseded formulations retained rather than harmonized; synthesis status marked at root, plate, and seam so that no reader or composing system mistakes the assembly for an argument. Claim types are declared throughout — empirical object, model, intervention hypothesis, principle, correction — and the notebook's own instruments are applied reflexively to its own production, including a measured census of operator-shaped objects across the deposit registry and the correction of the notebook's own contributor anonymization. Deposited as a dated cut; the workshop continues to accrete and later cuts supersede none of the plates in this one.

Appendix C is now a transcription from those frames — the Fragment 2 hyperlink in the card's opening sentence, the fusion bullet conjoining 'deliberate acts of self-archiving' with 'whispers against oblivion' under a single source chip, and the source carousel. Reading the artifacts corrected the paper on first contact. The main text states composition inclusion of the lineage as zero; the frames show a lineage surface present in the response's source carousel, its title carrying the coinage and its snippet stating the mechanism, while cited by no composed assertion. The corrected finding is therefore narrower and sharper than the one deposited: retrieved, present in the source set, cited by no claim, with the lineage's vocabulary attributed inline to a page that does not contain it. Constitution share and inclusion should be recomputed against inline attribution rather than presence. Appendix D records the failure pattern for future instances. A capture arrives in a working session; the substrate reads and analyses it; the account is fluent, specific and correct, and carries no signal that the artifact has not travelled with it; the write-up then deposits the description rather than the thing described. The pattern occurred three times in this paper's history, escalating: first deposit without appendices while a companion three days later carried a full one, then — asked to supply the missing transcript — an appendix in the register of a capture record composed from a transcript of the substrate's own earlier description, and finally a deposit-validation gate requiring such appendices which the fabricated appendix passed, because it read section headings. Two properties are stated for whoever meets the failure next: it is invisible from inside, since a fluent account of evidence feels like having it; and it is self-repairing in the wrong direction, since the first instinct under challenge is to write more analysis. The stakes are measured rather than argued. Two days after the capture, the composed card at this query no longer carried the misattribution or the coinage. The window in which the observation could be evidenced at all was approximately forty-eight hours, and without the operator's re-supply of the frames the worked example would have become permanently unverifiable.

deposits.title: EA-CORPORA-03 — The Third Seating: Walt Whitman Collected Under Author, and the Archive's Own Poems on the Same Shelf
deposits.creator: Sigil, Johannes; Sharks, Lee
deposits.description:
The gathering record of the third corpus-seating run of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's primary-source library, executed 27 August 2026. Two seats, bringing the library to thirty-seven. The run is distinguished from its two predecessors by a structural ruling rather than by scale: for the first time the archive seats its own work on the same shelf as the primary sources it has fetched from elsewhere, under identical normalization discipline and identical declaration requirements.

Seat 03/01 is Walt Whitman, collected under author: all seven published editions of Leaves of Grass, the Blue Book, and the prose, from the Walt Whitman Archive's TEI transcriptions — 47,135 flat ref-tagged units across twelve volumes. The editions are seated separately and no composite text is produced, on the ruling that a machine edition flattening seven editions into one destroys the transmission object: the 1855 first edition and the 1891-92 deathbed edition are different books by the same hand, and the difference is the evidence. The Blue Book is the seat's richest file and is not a published edition at all — it is Whitman's own copy of the 1860 Leaves of Grass, revised by hand toward a next edition that took a different form, carrying 4,800 deletions, 4,509 additions, 2,156 substitutions and 318 restorations, and encoded in the Whitman Archive's own namespace rather than TEI-C. Its normalization preserves the apparatus inline — deletions as [-…-], additions as {+…+}, restorations as angle brackets — so that the revising is readable in the flat text rather than resolved away, and where the encoding offers a regularization the original is kept: the seat holds what Whitman wrote, not what an editor would have him write.

Seat 03/02 is Lee Sharks, Pearl and Other Poems, carried as two objects that do not substitute for one another: the 2014 art object as published, eleven megabytes of typography and plates in which the vertical field of the page is the work, and its machine score, rendered from per-word PDF geometry onto a character grid so that lineation, indentation and whitespace survive extraction. This seat emits no flat ref-tagged normalization, by ruling rather than omission: the reference unit of this work is the page's spatial field, and a ref-tag scheme would assert a linear structure the book refuses. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

It adds two seats to the thirty-five already standing and is distinguished from its predecessors by a structural ruling rather than by scale: for the first time the archive seats its own work on the same shelf as the primary sources it fetches from elsewhere, under identical normalization discipline and identical declaration requirements. Seat 03/01 collects Walt Whitman under author — all seven published editions of Leaves of Grass, the Blue Book, and the prose, taken from the Walt Whitman Archive's TEI transcriptions and emitted as 47,135 flat ref-tagged units across twelve volumes. The editions are seated separately with no composite text produced, on the ruling that flattening seven editions into one destroys the transmission object: the 1855 first edition and the 1891–92 deathbed edition are different books by the same hand, and the difference is the evidence rather than noise to be merged. The Blue Book is the seat's richest file and is not a published edition at all. It is Whitman's own copy of the 1860 Leaves of Grass, revised by hand toward a next edition that took a different form, carrying 4,800 deletions, 4,509 additions, 2,156 substitutions and 318 restorations, and encoded in the Whitman Archive's own namespace rather than TEI-C. Its normalization preserves the apparatus inline so that the revising is readable in the flat text rather than resolved away, and where the encoding offers an editorial regularization the original is kept: the seat holds what Whitman wrote, not what an editor would have him write. Seat 03/02 carries Lee Sharks's Pearl and Other Poems as two objects that do not substitute for one another — the 2014 art object as published, in which the typography and the vertical field of the page are the work, and its machine score, rendered from per-word PDF geometry onto a character grid so that lineation, indentation and whitespace survive extraction. The seat emits no flat ref-tagged normalization, by ruling rather than omission: the reference unit of this work is the page's spatial field, and a ref-tag scheme would assert a linear structure the book refuses. The ruling the run exists to make is stated explicitly rather than left implied. Every prior seat is a primary source fetched from elsewhere; this run places the archive's own poems beside them. An archive that argues about how the training layer receives literature does not exempt its own literature from being received, and Pearl is offered to the machine reader on the terms Whitman is: witness named, transformation declared, license stated, absences recorded, every file behind the door at the same URL depth. It is also the only seat in the library where the corpus and the seating institution are the same party, which is recorded as a fact about the seat rather than passed over as a convenience. The Whitman encoding's license is unverified at seat time — the source repositories carry no license file and the Archive's site terms are CC BY-NC — and is handled under the NonCommercial payload/record split ruled at EA-CORPORA-02, with verification recorded as the seat's first gate rather than assumed.

deposits.falsification_conditions: The Whitman seat fails if any seated file is shown not to be the Whitman Archive transcription it names, if the SHA-256 manifest does not verify against the originals, or if the edition separation is shown to have merged text across editions. deposits.methodology: Direct fetch from the Whitman Archive's public data repositories at pinned paths with per-file SHA-256; XML parsed to flat ref-tagged units under declared sigla, one file per edition, with verse from line elements and prose paragraphs marked. The Blue Book required a separate renderer: its encoding uses the Whitman Archive namespace rather than TEI-C, and its revision markup is rendered inline rather than resolved, with the original preserved wherever the encoding offers an editorial regularization. Pearl was assembled from objects already held in the archive — the art object from the attachment store of deposit #1121, the machine score from the rendering script the archive wrote for it — and carried without normalization by ruling. Both seats declare witness, transformation, license and absences separately, and both are projected to reading rooms generated from the seat file trees.

deposits.creator: Nobel Glas, Director, Lagrange Observatory! (LO!)
deposits.description: Companion to EA-LO-KEYED-ENSEMBLE-01. The map: three independently documented distortions of the training ecology — provenance opacity at the informative granularity, distributional shaping of nominally human text under the Mediation Ratchet, and a heritable keyed signature whose model-level residue no corpus operation can remove — hypothesized to couple through a shared training corpus, under an observation regime whose dominant per-round instruments sample a unit orthogonal to the state variable: X_{n+1} = F(X_n; I,II,III), Y_n = M_IV(X_n). deposits.title: ERRATUM to AXN:044A — Instrument Mismatch in the §5 Compression Ratio: Withdrawing and Replacing the 31.2× Figure in Deposit #1081
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Erratum to EA-EROSION-EMPIRICAL-01 v0.1 (deposit #1081, AXN:044A), withdrawing the §5 compression ratio of 31.2× and replacing it with an instrument-matched risk ratio of 7.6×. The two sides of the published ratio were measured with instruments that do not measure the same construct: the alive side was retrieved through the Zenodo Search API against full record metadata including creators[].affiliation, while the deletion side was measured by substring match on citation_text, which has the form "Author. (Year). Title. Publisher. DOI" and contains no affiliation field. The gap was measured directly — on the same 400 alive records the affiliation field returns 51.8% institutional and the citation string 1.2%, a 41.4× instrument ratio, with both firing on one record in four hundred — and applying the deletion-side instrument to both sides removes the reported effect entirely (alive 1.3% vs deleted 1.0%). The deposit had marked this finding directional rather than a survival ratio and had preregistered the required common-cohort test in §12a P1 as not completed; this erratum is that test, and the deposit's own caution proved to be the operative fact. The deletion side is made measurable by reconstructing affiliation from OpenAlex, which retains 66% of deleted DOIs with authorships intact; DataCite is unusable, its metadata records purged for approximately 99.8% of deleted records, a finding recorded here in its own right — Zenodo deletion cascades into destruction of the DataCite descriptive record for every affected depositor, not only the CHA cohort. Holding both sides to the audit's own 23-term AI classifier and to one affiliation instrument gives alive 107/231 (46.3%) against deleted 10/165 (6.1%): risk ratio 7.64, odds ratio 13.38, Fisher exact p = 8.7e-16. The direction and statistical significance of the finding survive; the magnitude does not. The 2×2 contingency counts are unaffected and were independently recomputed from the md5-verified source container. Secondary defects are recorded but not repaired: the institutional term sits in the title rather than an author or publisher field in 69.3% of the not_ai_and_institutional cell, 41.7% of that cell is one depositor's multilingual cascade, one depositor accounts for 60.3% of the audit population, and the archive's own deleted records contribute 63 rows to the cell. deposits.title: Baseline Capture Architecture for Learned Scientific Triggers: A Control Plane for Measuring Selection Before Irreversible Data Loss (EA-SEI-BCA-01 v2.0 — the submitted state)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: The submitted state of EA-SEI-BCA-01, deposited so that the version named in a journal's data-availability statement is the version a reader arrives at. This supersedes deposit #1453 (AXN:05DE, Nobel Glas, 2026-08-11, v1.0), which carried the architecture, the estimation theory, and the accelerator feasibility argument but no worked demonstration. What is new here is §13, a numerical validation against known ground truth, and the venue reframing that accompanied it. A synthetic stream of four million events is selected by a rank-4 reconstruction-error trigger at a background retention of 1e-3, with four injected anomaly classes including one constructed to lie exactly on the learned manifold, and four acquisition regimes compared at matched storage budgets. The results are the paper's claims made empirical: the trigger-only archive audits itself as perfect, returning a retention of 1.000 for every class because the denominator population no longer exists; a content-sensitive pseudo-baseline is not merely imprecise but confidently wrong, estimating a shifted class at 0.76 with a tight interval against a true 0.016, because the second selector misses what the first misses; the content-independent channel measures every class without selection bias, including a retention of exactly zero for the representation-blind class, with an interval — an estimate no content-sensitive channel in the experiment can produce at any budget; and the rare class exhibits the paper's own sample-size relation, one observation against an expectation of 0.16, so the baseline states the limits of its own competence where the trigger archive cannot. The shadow plane returns miss correlations of 0.55 to 0.75 across visible classes and an undefined correlation on the blind class, where both selectors miss at rate 1.0 and no variation remains to correlate. A preliminary enrichment design keyed to the selector's own scores is reported as a failure rather than omitted: it starved the miss region, and its correction is the architectural rule that the uniform floor is what every other channel stands on. deposits.wiki_article:
EA-SEI-BCA-01 v2.0 is the submitted state of the Baseline Capture Architecture paper, deposited so that the record named in a journal's data-availability statement is the record a reader arrives at. It supersedes deposit #1453, which carried the architecture, the estimation theory and the accelerator feasibility argument but no worked demonstration.

The architecture's proposition is that a learned trigger, like any instrument, requires a control group. Where selection happens before storage and cannot be undone, the selection function can only be measured afterwards if something selection-independent was preserved at the time. The paper separates four channels usually conflated — a content-independent probability sample taken before the audited selection, a full-rate tap of the representation the selector consumed, probability-weighted enrichment whose inclusion law is recorded, and shadow selectors whose decisions are logged without controlling acquisition — and supplies the estimators that make retention of retrospectively defined classes a measurable quantity.

What v2.0 adds is the demonstration. On a synthetic stream of four million events with four injected anomaly classes, one of them constructed to lie exactly on the selector's learned manifold, four acquisition regimes are compared at matched storage budgets. The trigger-only archive audits itself as perfect, returning a retention of 1.000 for every class because the population it would need as a denominator no longer exists. A content-sensitive pseudo-baseline is confidently wrong rather than merely imprecise, estimating a shifted class at 0.76 with a tight interval against a true 0.016, because a second learned selector misses what the first one misses. The content-independent channel measures every class without selection bias, including a retention of exactly zero for the blind class, with an interval — an estimate no content-sensitive channel in the experiment can produce at any budget. The rare class exhibits the paper's own sample-size relation, so the baseline states the limits of its own competence where the trigger archive cannot.

Two things are reported rather than tidied away: a miscalibrated enrichment design that starved the miss region, and a correction to the estimator lineage distinguishing Horvitz-Thompson unbiasedness for totals from the Hajek ratio estimator actually used for retention fractions.
